name: FOLDTRACE active-site benchmark
description: Data and analysis deposit for the FOLDTRACE active-site benchmark. FOLDTRACE reads the state of a known active site directly from a predicted protein structure: it superposes a candidate on a reference with TM-align, follows the order-preserving residue correspondence to each chemistry-defining position, and classifies that position as retained, altered, lost, or unresolved. This deposit contains the benchmark used to evaluate it, together with every intermediate needed to check or repeat that evaluation. The benchmark is prospectively frozen. Sixty-two experimentally characterised proteins from ten unrelated families were selected, and their reference structures, chemistry-defining positions, classification rules and expected states were fixed and recorded before any method was run. Thirty-seven retain the reference active-site state, two carry an experimentally established alteration, and twenty-three have lost the chemistry-defining residues. Every expected state is supported by a traceable primary experimental source. That freeze can be verified rather than taken on trust. FREEZE.md records the lock time (2026-08-25T09:39:10Z) together with SHA256 hashes of the benchmark plan, the target manifest and the evidence sources. A verification script using only the Python standard library re-hashes those files and reports whether they are the files that were locked.
